# @zakkster/lite-logn

Version: 0.13.0
License: MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev <shinikchiev@yahoo.com>
Runtime dependencies: none. ESM only. ASCII-only source. sideEffects: false.
Node: >= 18.

## What it is

A tree-shakeable, zero-GC family of O(log n) data structures that PROVES its
logarithm instead of asserting it. The complexity class is the product: every
hot op is O(log n) worst-case (or expected / amortized where stated) and
allocates zero bytes after construction, and a shipped witness harness fits
`nsPerOp = intercept + slope * log2(n)` and demonstrates the straight log line
against a built-in O(n) foil that leaves it.

It is the O(log n) sibling of @zakkster/lite-o1: lite-o1 holds the constant (a
FLAT ops/ms line on a log-x axis), lite-logn holds the logarithm (a STRAIGHT
line on that same axis, one added level per doubling of n).

v0.1.0 shipped BinaryHeap; v0.2.0 adds Fenwick; v0.3.0 adds SegmentTree; v0.4.0
adds SkipList; v0.5.0 adds Treap; v0.6.0 adds Scapegoat; v0.7.0 adds MinMaxHeap;
v0.8.0 adds SplayTree; v0.9.0 adds BinomialHeap; v0.10.0 adds PairingHeap; v0.11.0
adds FibonacciHeap (the mergeable-heap arc's FINALE); v0.12.0 adds Fenwick2D (the
family's FIRST 2D structure); v0.13.0 adds SegmentTree2D (the general 2D rectangle
fold -- min/max/sum/gcd -- a 2D BIT cannot do). The roster (one member per session,
each landing append-only):

- BinaryHeap (v0.1.0)  -- an INDEXED binary heap (addressable priority queue): a
  min|max binary heap over three parallel typed arrays (`_key` Float64Array,
  `_id` Uint32Array, `_pos` Int32Array reverse map) with children at 2i+1 / 2i+2.
  push / pop / changeKey / remove are O(log n); peek / topKey / keyOf / has are
  O(1); nothing allocated per op. The reverse-index map makes changeKey / remove
  addressable by a caller-supplied entity id. The cleanest witness in the family
  and the one that calibrates the shared R^2 floor + slope band gate (pop).
- Fenwick / BIT (v0.2.0) -- BOTH point-update AND prefix-sum in O(log n) over a
  single flat `Float64Array` via the lowest-set-bit walk (`i & -i`); rangeSum is
  two prefix walks. 0-based public indices; 1-based internally (`_t[0]` the unused
  identity sentinel). Two straight log lines (update + prefix).
- SegmentTree (v0.3.0) -- general associative range-query (min / max / sum / gcd)
  + point-update over a SINGLE flat `Float64Array(2n)` (leaves at n..2n-1, `_t[0]`
  unused), BOTH O(log n) via iterative bottom-up walks; the fold is chosen ONCE at
  construction (ctor-cached small-int `_k` combined by an inline switch). The
  complement to Fenwick: Fenwick's rangeSum needs an INVERSE (subtraction), so it
  is sum-only; SegmentTree folds any associative + commutative op over a range.
- SkipList (v0.4.0) -- a pointer-free ordered map (key -> value): get / set /
  delete / successor / predecessor / rangeIter, EXPECTED O(log n) via a
  probabilistic tower of forward links stored as slot INDICES in flat Uint32Array
  columns (`NIL = 0`, slot 0 the head sentinel) over a PRIVATE free-list (NodePool,
  design-parity with lite-o1's private pools, NOT a runtime dep). Level generation
  is one NR-LCG step, HIGH bits -> geometric height (`1 + clz32`), instance-local
  seed, deterministic. set updates an existing key's value in place. EXPECTED (not
  worst-case) O(log n): the witness fits the average line AND prints the MAX single
  insert. Zero allocation on every hot op.
- Treap (v0.5.0) -- an AUGMENTED ordered map (key -> value) that is also an order-
  statistic tree: a randomized, self-balancing BST (BST order on keys x max-heap order
  on a per-node random priority -> EXPECTED O(log n) height) with a subtree-size column
  that adds rank(x) (count of keys < x) / select(k) (the k-th smallest key) / split(key)
  / merge(a, b), all EXPECTED O(log n). Nodes are slot INDICES in flat typed-array
  columns (_key / _value / _left / _right / _prio / _size) over the SAME private free-
  list (NodePool) SkipList uses. Priority is one instance-local NR-LCG draw per insert
  (deterministic, seed-reproducible; ties break by key). set updates an existing key's
  value in place. split / merge REWIRE in place (O(log n)) so the two treaps SHARE a
  backing arena and CONSUME their inputs. EXPECTED, not worst-case: the MAX single
  insert (rotation chain) is DISCLOSED, never gated. Zero allocation on every hot op.
- Scapegoat (v0.6.0) -- a DETERMINISTIC, weight-balanced AUGMENTED ordered map (key ->
  value) that is also an order-statistic tree -- the honest PAIR to Treap. get is
  WORST-case O(log n) (a hard height bound <= log_{1/alpha}(n) + 1, never merely
  expected); set / delete are AMORTIZED O(log n) (an occasional subtree rebuild absorbs
  the imbalance). A subtree-size column adds rank(x) / select(k), O(log n). NO priorities,
  NO RNG anywhere: the shape is a deterministic function of the insert / delete order.
  Nodes are slot INDICES in flat typed-array columns (_key / _value / _left / _right /
  _size) over the SAME private free-list (NodePool); the ZERO-GC rebuild reuses ONE
  preallocated scratch buffer (_flat) + ONE preallocated index-stack (_stack) -- an
  iterative Morris-free flatten + a bounded log-depth balanced rebuild on the native
  stack -- so even a rebuild-heavy trace is 0 B/op. alpha is frozen at construction in the
  OPEN interval (0.55, 0.75) (both ends throw); default 2/3. Unlike Treap there is NO
  split / merge (no priority heap to merge by; an honest deterministic split/merge would
  be O(n) rebuilds) -- the documented asymmetry vs Treap. set updates an existing key's
  value in place. The amortized-trace witness shows cumulative insert cost/op tracks log n
  despite the rebuild spikes. Zero allocation on every hot op.
- MinMaxHeap (v0.7.0) -- a DOUBLE-ENDED priority queue (DEPQ) held in ONE array-embedded
  binary heap whose levels ALTERNATE min / max (Atkinson et al. 1986). Even depth is a MIN
  level, odd depth a MAX level, so the minimum is the root and the maximum is the LARGER of
  the root's up-to-two children: peekMin / peekMax are O(1); push / popMin / popMax are all
  WORST-case O(log n) from that single heap (no second heap, no paired-heap correspondence).
  Two parallel typed-array columns (`_key` Float64, `_id` Uint32) in the BinaryHeap id+key
  idiom; the id is an OPAQUE Uint32 payload in [0, 2^32) (NOT unique, no reverse map), so
  there is deliberately NO changeKey / remove -- the documented asymmetry vs BinaryHeap.
  Level parity is `((31 - Math.clz32(i + 1)) & 1) === 0` (min iff even depth), computed
  zero-alloc; the sifts are hole-punching (one write per level). Keys are finite numbers
  (typeof-guarded before coercion; Symbol / BigInt / NaN / +-Infinity fail closed). This is
  the classic one-element-per-node min-max heap only; the interval-heap DEPQ is deferred.
  Zero allocation on every hot op.

- SplayTree (v0.8.0) -- a SELF-ADJUSTING BST ordered map (key -> value) whose every access
  RESTRUCTURES the tree so the touched key becomes the root (an iterative TOP-DOWN splay,
  Sleator & Tarjan 1985). Recently / frequently used keys ride near the top, giving AMORTIZED
  O(log n) per op and genuinely FASTER-than-log behaviour on skewed / working-set access. It
  keeps NO balance metadata: four typed-array columns (`_key` / `_value` Float64, `_left` /
  `_right` Uint32) over the same private free-list (NodePool); slot 0 is the NIL sentinel AND
  the splay's dummy header, with two fixed scratch hands (`_hl` / `_hr`) -- so the splay uses
  NO parent column, NO path stack and NO recursion (0 B/op, no chain can overflow the stack).
  A READ MUTATES: get / has / successor / predecessor SPLAY and bump the iteration version, so
  an in-flight rangeIter fails closed even on a read; rangeIter / forEach / [Symbol.iterator]
  are NON-splaying in-order walks (re-descend by key each step, leave _root + _version byte-
  identical) -- so they cost O(n * depth) (forEach / iterator) or O((k+1) * depth) (rangeIter):
  O(n log n) on a balanced / used tree, but O(n^2) on a COLD tree built by pure sorted insertion
  with no intervening access (splay a key, or insert in mixed order, to keep it shallow before a
  full walk). delete splays the target up then JOINS its subtrees (splay the max of the left
  subtree, hang the right subtree off it). AMORTIZED + DETERMINISTIC (no RNG): a single cold
  deep access can splay an O(n) chain, DISCLOSED by the witness, never gated. This is the LEAN
  member: deliberately NO rank / select / split / merge (the documented asymmetry vs Treap /
  Scapegoat). Keys and values are finite numbers (typeof-guarded before coercion; Symbol /
  BigInt / NaN / +-Infinity fail closed). Zero allocation on every hot op.

- BinomialHeap (v0.9.0) -- the family's first MERGEABLE priority queue: a forest of heap-
  ordered binomial trees whose defining op is `meld` (union two heaps) in O(log n) WORST-case
  via a BINARY CARRY over the two order-sorted root lists (the structural analogue of adding
  two binary numbers). push is O(1) AMORTIZED (O(log n) worst), popMin is O(log n) worst
  (unlink the extreme root, reverse its child list into a new root list, union back, rescan the
  O(log n) roots), and peekMin is O(1) via a cached `_min` root maintained INLINE (never
  rescanned on the hot path). Six pointer-free typed-array columns (`_key` Float64, `_id`
  Uint32, `_parent` / `_child` / `_sibling` / `_order` Uint32) over a private free-list
  (NodePool); NIL = 0 reserves slot 0. LEAN + NON-ADDRESSABLE (the MinMaxHeap idiom): the id is
  an OPAQUE Uint32 payload in [0, 2^32) (not unique, no reverse map), so there is deliberately
  NO decreaseKey / remove / changeKey / rank / select. SHARED-ARENA meld: a meld rewires roots
  in place, so two heaps can meld only if they draw from the SAME arena -- a standalone
  `new BinomialHeap(capacity, kind)` owns its own arena, `BinomialHeap.arena(capacity, kind,
  count)` hands out `count` arena-sharing heaps. `a.meld(b)` CONSUMES b: b becomes empty (size
  0) and DEAD -- every later op on b throws `[lite-logn]` rather than silently re-enter the now-
  shared roots (the Treap.split/merge consume idiom, hardened with a consumed flag). Cross-arena
  detection is column identity (`a._key !== b._key`); a kind mismatch, a non-BinomialHeap arg,
  a self-meld, or a consumed operand each throw. kind 'min' | 'max' frozen at construction.
  Keys are finite numbers (typeof-guarded before coercion; Symbol / BigInt / NaN / +-Infinity
  fail closed). forEach / [Symbol.iterator] yield ids in UNSPECIFIED (forest) order. Zero
  allocation on every hot op.

- PairingHeap (v0.10.0) -- the mergeable-heap arc's ADDRESSABLE member: a single multi-way
  heap-ordered tree (left-child / right-sibling) whose defining ops are a cut-and-link
  `decreaseKey` (AMORTIZED O(log n)) and an O(1) `meld`. push / peekMin / peekMinKey / meld are
  O(1); popMin / decreaseKey / remove are AMORTIZED O(log n). popMin unlinks the root then does a
  TWO-PASS combine of the root's child list (pair left-to-right, then fold right-to-left) --
  iterative and POINTER-FREE, the sibling links ARE the work list, so NO temporary array (0 B/op).
  LOUD CONTRACT DIFFERENCE vs BinomialHeap: PairingHeap is ADDRESSABLE with ARENA-WIDE-UNIQUE ids
  -- caller ids are unique integers in [0, capacity), and the reverse map `_pos` (id -> slot) is
  SHARED across EVERY heap drawing the arena (BinomialHeap's ids are opaque, non-unique, no
  reverse map). Each slot carries an `_owner` tag so decreaseKey(id) / remove(id) on an id owned
  by a DIFFERENT live sibling heap is O(1)-detected and throws `[lite-logn]` (never a silent
  cross-heap cut); pushing an id live ANYWHERE in the arena throws (arena-wide uniqueness). Five
  pointer-free typed-array columns (`_key` Float64, `_id` / `_child` / `_sibling` / `_parent`
  Uint32 -- `_parent` is a dual-role PREV pointer that makes cut O(1)) + the arena-wide `_pos`
  Int32 reverse map + a per-slot `_owner` + a union-find `_alias` over heap ids, over a private
  free-list (NodePool); NIL = 0 reserves slot 0. SHARED-ARENA meld is O(1): a single root-link +
  a union alias redirecting the donor's heap id to the melder's (INDEPENDENT of |donor| -- BETTER
  than BinomialHeap's O(log n) meld), so a melded-in id is still reprioritizable via the surviving
  heap WITHOUT re-tagging every node (a per-heap map would make meld O(|donor|), the rejected
  alternative). `a.meld(b)` CONSUMES b (empty, size 0, DEAD -- every later op throws). Cross-arena
  detection is column identity (`a._key !== b._key`); a kind mismatch, a non-PairingHeap arg, a
  self-meld, or a consumed operand each throw. `decreaseKey` operates TOWARD the heap's extreme
  (decrease for 'min', increase for 'max'); a move away fails closed. kind 'min' | 'max' frozen at
  construction. Keys are finite numbers (typeof-guarded before coercion; Symbol / BigInt / NaN /
  +-Infinity fail closed). forEach / [Symbol.iterator] yield ids in UNSPECIFIED (forest) order.
  Zero allocation on every hot op.

- FibonacciHeap (v0.11.0) -- the mergeable-heap arc's FINALE: the textbook-optimal ADDRESSABLE
  mergeable priority queue. push / meld / decreaseKey are O(1) AMORTIZED; popMin / remove are
  O(log n) AMORTIZED. Same ADDRESSABLE, ARENA-WIDE-UNIQUE-id + shared-`_pos` reverse-map + per-slot
  `_owner` + union-find `_alias` contract as PairingHeap (a sibling-owned decreaseKey/remove fails
  closed; a live-anywhere id cannot be re-pushed). Where PairingHeap reaches the amortized bounds
  with a lean two-pass combine (and usually WINS wall-clock), FibonacciHeap reaches them by the full
  textbook machine: a lazy forest of heap-ordered trees on CIRCULAR doubly-linked `_left`/`_right`
  lists (root list AND each child list circular), a `decreaseKey` that CUTS a node's subtree to the
  root and CASCADES up its former parent chain (a marked parent is cut too; the first unmarked
  non-root parent is marked and the walk stops) governed by a per-node `_mark` Uint8 column, and a
  `popMin` that splices the min root's children into the root list then CONSOLIDATES by degree via a
  preallocated per-arena degree bucket (`_bucket` Uint32, sized to the GOLDEN-RATIO degree bound
  D(n) <= log_phi n ~ 1.44 log2 n -- ceil(log2 cap) would undersize it -- and cleared per call in
  O(maxDegree), never left stale). Eight pointer-free columns (`_key` Float64, `_id` / `_left` /
  `_right` / `_child` / `_parent` / `_degree` Uint32, `_mark` Uint8) + the arena-wide `_pos` Int32 +
  per-slot `_owner` + union-find `_alias` + the `_bucket` scratch, over a private free-list
  (NodePool); NIL = 0 reserves slot 0. SHARED-ARENA meld is O(1): concatenate the two circular root
  lists + a union alias redirecting the donor's heap id to the melder's (INDEPENDENT of |donor|, no
  per-node retag) + a cached-extreme update; `a.meld(b)` CONSUMES b (empty, size 0, DEAD). The
  cascade is ITERATIVE (a native loop, no recursion) so decreaseKey stays 0 B/op. HONESTY: this
  member is textbook-optimal in ASYMPTOTICS but OFTEN SLOWER wall-clock than Pairing/Binary on real
  hardware (large constant factors); the witness DISCLOSES the MAX single popMin AND the MAX single
  decreaseKey (the cascading-cut spike) and does NOT gate them. Its witness R^2 (popMin) gates on
  the MEDIAN of independent sweep-fits: a single fit's R^2 can dip below the 0.958 floor in a
  minority of runs, the median clears it reliably -- no unreproducible "every run" claim is made.
  kind 'min' | 'max' frozen at construction; keys are finite numbers (typeof-guarded before
  coercion). forEach / [Symbol.iterator] yield ids in UNSPECIFIED (forest) order. Zero allocation
  on every hot op.

- Fenwick2D (v0.12.0) -- the family's FIRST 2D / multi-dimensional member: a 2D Binary Indexed Tree
  that lifts the 1D Fenwick's lowest-set-bit walk to a rectangle. BOTH point-update AND 2D-prefix
  (and therefore arbitrary axis-aligned RECTANGLE sums via inclusion-exclusion) in O(log^2 n) =
  O(log rows * log cols) over a SINGLE flat `Float64Array((rows+1)*(cols+1))` -- row 0 / col 0 the
  unused identity sentinels, 1-based internally, 0-based public coords. update climbs BOTH dims by
  `i & -i` (an outer rows loop, an inner cols loop, one `_t` touch per (i, j) level pair); prefix
  descends both dims; rectSum inlines the 2D inclusion-exclusion `P(r2,c2) - P(r1-1,c2) - P(r2,c1-1)
  + P(r1-1,c1-1)` (r1 == 0 / c1 == 0 zero their terms by a k = 0 loop-skip -- never a prefix(-1)
  read). Dims frozen at ctor; `F2D_MAX_CELLS = 0x7FFFFFFF` caps (rows+1)*(cols+1), guarded by a
  FLOAT multiply (never `| 0`, which would wrap a large product to a small int and fail OPEN).
  Fenwick2D.build(matrix) is O(rows*cols) LINEAR in TWO SEPARATE passes (cols within each row, then
  rows) -- fusing them double-counts. Values are finite numbers (negatives allowed; typeof-guarded
  before coercion; NaN / +-Infinity / non-number / Symbol / BigInt fail closed). SUM-ONLY and
  index-addressed (the 1D Fenwick's boundary, lifted): deliberately NO 2D min / max / gcd (a BIT has
  no inverse for them -- a future 2D SegmentTree) and NO changeKey / rank / select. WORST-CASE (no
  max-single-op line). This member's witness is the family's FIRST on a SQUARED-log axis
  ((log2 n)^2). Zero allocation on every hot op.

- SegmentTree2D (v0.13.0) -- the general 2D rectangle FOLD a 2D BIT cannot do: a segment tree OF
  segment trees (a tree of trees) that folds min / max / sum / gcd over any axis-aligned rectangle,
  BOTH point-update AND rectangle-query in O(log^2 n) = O(log rows * log cols) over a SINGLE flat
  `Float64Array(4 * rows * cols)`. SegmentTree2D : Fenwick2D :: SegmentTree (1D) : Fenwick (1D) --
  it lifts the exact rectangle MIN / MAX / GCD Fenwick2D lists as its documented not-for. The fold
  is chosen ONCE at ctor (small-int `_k`, inline switch, no closure). update writes the leaf, climbs
  the leaf ROW's col-tree at column c, THEN climbs the ROW-tree -- at each row-ancestor it recomputes
  the changed leaf column from its two row-children FIRST, then fixes that row-node's col-tree up
  column c's path (the inner-then-outer order is the correctness site). query descends the OUTER row
  dim half-open collecting O(log rows) boundary row-nodes and does an INNER col-range fold over each
  (double `l&1`/`r&1` picks in both dims), all into one identity-seeded accumulator. Correct ONLY for
  COMMUTATIVE + associative folds (the iterative 2n layout is order-agnostic). Identity fills cleared
  / unused cells and is a legal RESULT (a cleared min grid queries +Infinity) but never a legal INPUT
  (NaN / +-Infinity fail closed typeof-first; the gcd kind also rejects negatives / non-integers).
  Dims frozen at ctor; `S2D_MAX_CELLS = 0x7FFFFFFF` caps 4*rows*cols, guarded by a FLOAT multiply
  (never `| 0`, which would wrap a large product to a small int and fail OPEN -> OOB). SegmentTree2D
  .build(matrix, kind) is O(rows*cols) two-phase (fold each row's col-tree, THEN fold the row-tree
  position-wise) -- NOT rows*cols updates. SPACE co-headline: 4*rows*cols cells, ~4x a 2D BIT's
  (rows+1)*(cols+1) -- the honest price for the general (non-invertible) folds. WORST-CASE (no
  max-single-op line); its witness is the family's SECOND on the SQUARED-log axis ((log2 n)^2). Zero
  allocation on every hot op.

## Exports (from the single main file LogN.js)

- `VERSION` -- string. The package version; one of the three version sites
  (package.json / LogN.js VERSION const / this file's `Version:` header).
- `BinaryHeap` -- class. An indexed binary heap (addressable priority queue).
  - `new BinaryHeap(capacity, kind = 'min')` -- capacity is an integer in
    [1, 2^31-1]; kind is 'min' or 'max'. Allocates the three typed arrays once.
  - `push(id, key)` -> void. id integer in [0, capacity), not already present;
    key finite. Throws on out-of-range/duplicate id, non-finite key, full heap.
  - `pop()` -> id | undefined. Removes the extremum; undefined if empty (no throw).
  - `peek()` -> id | undefined. `topKey()` -> key | undefined. Read-only.
  - `keyOf(id)` -> key | undefined. `has(id)` -> boolean. Out-of-range id throws.
  - `changeKey(id, newKey)` -> void. Reprioritize a present entity (auto-direction
    sift); a non-member id throws (never a silent no-op).
  - `remove(id)` -> boolean. Idempotent: false if absent, true if removed.
  - `size` / `capacity` / `kind` getters; `clear()`; `forEach(fn)` and
    `[Symbol.iterator]()` yield live ids in UNSPECIFIED (heap-array) order -- NOT
    sorted / pop order.
  - `BinaryHeap.build(kind, ids, keys, capacity)` -> BinaryHeap. Floyd O(n) bulk
    build from parallel arrays; fails closed on duplicate/out-of-range id,
    non-finite key, or count > capacity.

- `Fenwick` -- class. A Fenwick tree (Binary Indexed Tree): BOTH point-update AND
  prefix-sum in O(log n) over a single flat `Float64Array` via the lowest-set-bit
  walk (`i & -i`). Public indices 0-based in [0, length); internally 1-based
  (`_t[0]` the unused identity sentinel -- null is not zero). Values are finite
  numbers (negatives allowed); NaN / +-Infinity / non-number fail closed.
  - `new Fenwick(length)` -- length is an integer in [1, 2^31-1]. Allocates one
    `Float64Array(length + 1)`, zero-initialized.
  - `update(i, delta)` -> this. Add delta at 0-based index i (climb by `i & -i`);
    delta must be a finite number (typeof-guarded first); out-of-range i throws.
  - `prefix(i)` -> number. Sum of [0, i] INCLUSIVE (descend by `i & -i`).
    `prefix(-1) === 0` is the clean base case; valid domain [-1, length).
  - `rangeSum(lo, hi)` -> number. Sum of [lo, hi] INCLUSIVE both ends =
    prefix(hi) - prefix(lo-1); throws on out-of-range or lo > hi.
  - `at(i)` -> number. The single element = prefix(i) - prefix(i-1).
  - `set(i, value)` -> this. Set element i to value (absolute), via
    update(i, value - at(i)); value must be finite.
  - `length` getter; `clear()` -> this (zero-fill, keep capacity);
    `forEach(fn)` visits (value, index, fenwick) in ascending index order.
  - `Fenwick.build(values)` -> Fenwick. O(n) LINEAR bulk build (each cell adds
    itself to its parent in one pass -- NOT n incremental updates); fails closed
    on a non-array-like or any non-finite value.

- `SegmentTree` -- class. An associative range-query AND a point-update, BOTH
  O(log n), over a SINGLE flat `Float64Array(2n)` (leaves at n..2n-1, `_t[0]`
  unused). The fold (min / max / sum / gcd) is chosen ONCE at construction and
  cached as a small-int combined by an inline switch on the hot path. The
  iterative 2n layout is order-agnostic -- correct because all four folds are
  commutative + associative (a non-commutative fold would need a pow2 layout).
  Identity fills query accumulators + cleared / fresh leaves (sum -> 0, min ->
  +Infinity, max -> -Infinity, gcd -> 0) but is never a legal INPUT: the value
  door rejects user NaN / +-Infinity, and the gcd kind additionally rejects
  negatives + non-integers (typeof-guarded before coercion).
  - `new SegmentTree(length, kind)` -- length an integer in [1, 2^30-1] (HALF of
    Fenwick's ceiling: the 2n array must keep `2n` a positive int32); kind is
    'min' | 'max' | 'sum' | 'gcd'. Allocates one `Float64Array(2 * length)`.
  - `query(lo, hi)` -> number. The fold over [lo, hi] INCLUSIVE both ends; throws
    on out-of-range or lo > hi (matching Fenwick.rangeSum). lo == hi returns that
    single leaf. A fresh / cleared tree queries to the identity.
  - `update(i, value)` -> this. Set leaf i to value (ABSOLUTE), then fix ancestors;
    value finite (nonnegative integer for the gcd kind), out-of-range i throws.
  - `at(i)` -> number. The single leaf value. O(1). Out-of-range i throws.
  - `length` / `kind` getters; `clear()` -> this (reset to identity, keep
    capacity); `forEach(fn)` visits (value, index, tree) in ascending leaf order.
  - `SegmentTree.build(values, kind)` -> SegmentTree. O(n) bottom-up bulk build
    (seed leaves, then fold each internal node once deepest-first -- NOT n
    incremental updates); fails closed on a non-array-like, any non-finite value,
    or (gcd) any negative / non-integer.

- `SkipList` -- class. A pointer-free ordered map (key -> value) whose get / set /
  delete / successor / predecessor are EXPECTED O(log n) via a probabilistic tower
  of forward links stored as slot INDICES in a single flat `Uint32Array` of
  `columns * (capacity + 1)` cells (`NIL = 0`, slot 0 the head sentinel) over a
  PRIVATE free-list (NodePool) -- no heap object per op. Keys are finite numbers
  (typeof-guarded before coercion; Symbol / BigInt / NaN / +-Infinity fail closed);
  values are finite numbers. EXPECTED, not worst-case (an unlucky seed can spike one
  op; the witness prints the MAX single insert).
  - `new SkipList(capacity, seed?)` -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^26-1] (slot
    indices are Uint32, `NIL = 0` reserves slot 0); seed an unsigned 32-bit integer
    (default fixed). Level columns sized to ceil(log2 cap)+1 up front (never grown).
  - `get(key)` -> value | undefined. Absent -> undefined (no throw).
  - `set(key, value)` -> this. Insert, or update the value in place if key exists
    (no new node). Non-finite key/value throws; a full pool throws.
  - `delete(key)` -> boolean. Idempotent: false if absent, true if removed.
  - `successor(key)` -> key | undefined. Smallest key STRICTLY greater than key.
  - `predecessor(key)` -> key | undefined. Largest key STRICTLY less than key.
  - `rangeIter(lo, hi)` -> iterator of keys in [lo, hi] INCLUSIVE, ascending;
    VERSION-STAMPED (mutation mid-iteration throws). Bounds may be +-Infinity;
    NaN or lo > hi throws.
  - `size` / `capacity` getters; `clear()` -> this (empty, keep capacity, reset the
    PRNG to its initial seed); `forEach(fn)` visits (key, value, list) ascending.

- `Treap` -- class. A randomized-balanced AUGMENTED ordered map (key -> value) that is
  also an order-statistic tree. A BST on `_key` x a max-heap on a per-node random
  `_prio` gives EXPECTED O(log n) height; a `_size` subtree-count column adds O(log n)
  order statistics. Nodes are slot INDICES in flat typed-array columns (`_key` /
  `_value` Float64, `_left` / `_right` / `_prio` / `_size` Uint32, `NIL = 0`) over a
  PRIVATE free-list (NodePool) -- no heap object per op. Keys and values are finite
  numbers (typeof-guarded before coercion; Symbol / BigInt / NaN / +-Infinity fail
  closed). EXPECTED, not worst-case (an unlucky priority draw can spike one op; the MAX
  single insert is disclosed). set / delete / split / merge recurse to a depth = tree
  height (O(log n) expected, O(n) worst-case on a pathological priority draw), on the
  native call stack, so every hot op is still 0 B/op.
  - `new Treap(capacity, seed?)` -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^31-1] (slot indices +
    subtree counts are Uint32, `NIL = 0` reserves slot 0); seed an unsigned 32-bit
    integer (default fixed). Allocates six columns + a free-list once.
  - `get(key)` -> value | undefined. Absent -> undefined (no throw).
  - `has(key)` -> boolean.
  - `set(key, value)` -> this. Insert, or update the value in place if key exists (no
    new node). Non-finite key/value throws; a full pool throws.
  - `delete(key)` -> boolean. Idempotent: false if absent, true if removed.
  - `rank(x)` -> number. Count of stored keys STRICTLY LESS than x, in [0, size].
  - `select(k)` -> key | undefined. The k-th smallest key (0-based); undefined if k is
    out of [0, size). Non-integer k throws.
  - `successor(key)` -> key | undefined. Smallest key STRICTLY greater than key.
  - `predecessor(key)` -> key | undefined. Largest key STRICTLY less than key.
  - `rangeIter(lo, hi)` -> iterator of keys in [lo, hi] INCLUSIVE, ascending; VERSION-
    STAMPED (structural OR value mutation mid-iteration throws). Bounds may be
    +-Infinity; NaN or lo > hi throws.
  - `size` / `capacity` getters; `clear()` -> this (empty, keep capacity, reset the
    PRNG to its initial seed); `forEach(fn)` visits (key, value, treap) ascending.
  - `split(key)` -> [left, right]. left holds keys < key, right holds keys >= key;
    O(log n) EXPECTED (rewires in place), so the two treaps SHARE this treap's arena
    and this is CONSUMED (left empty).
  - `Treap.merge(a, b)` -> Treap. Merge two arena-sharing treaps where every key of a
    < every key of b; O(log n) EXPECTED, CONSUMES both. Non-Treap inputs, treaps from
    different arenas, or an overlapping key range each throw.

- `Scapegoat` -- class. A DETERMINISTIC, weight-balanced AUGMENTED ordered map (key ->
  value) that is also an order-statistic tree -- the honest PAIR to Treap. A BST on
  `_key` kept alpha-weight-balanced (get WORST-case O(log n); set / delete AMORTIZED
  O(log n) via an occasional subtree rebuild); a `_size` subtree-count column adds O(log n)
  order statistics. NO priorities, NO RNG. Nodes are slot INDICES in flat typed-array
  columns (`_key` / `_value` Float64, `_left` / `_right` / `_size` Uint32, `NIL = 0`) over
  a PRIVATE free-list (NodePool); the zero-GC rebuild reuses ONE preallocated `_flat`
  scratch + ONE `_stack` index-stack (iterative Morris-free flatten + bounded log-depth
  balanced rebuild on the native stack) -- no heap object, no fresh array, 0 B/op even
  under a rebuild storm. Keys and values are finite numbers (typeof-guarded before
  coercion; Symbol / BigInt / NaN / +-Infinity fail closed).
  - `new Scapegoat(capacity, alpha?)` -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^31-1] (slot indices
    + subtree counts are Uint32, `NIL = 0` reserves slot 0); alpha the weight-balance
    factor in the OPEN interval (0.55, 0.75) (both ends throw), frozen at construction;
    default 2/3. Allocates five columns + a free-list + two rebuild scratch buffers once.
  - `get(key)` -> value | undefined. Absent -> undefined (no throw).
  - `has(key)` -> boolean.
  - `set(key, value)` -> this. Insert, or update the value in place if key exists (no new
    node, no rebuild). Non-finite key/value throws; a full pool throws.
  - `delete(key)` -> boolean. Idempotent: false if absent, true if removed.
  - `rank(x)` -> number. Count of stored keys STRICTLY LESS than x, in [0, size].
  - `select(k)` -> key | undefined. The k-th smallest key (0-based); undefined if k is out
    of [0, size). Non-integer k throws.
  - `successor(key)` -> key | undefined. Smallest key STRICTLY greater than key.
  - `predecessor(key)` -> key | undefined. Largest key STRICTLY less than key.
  - `rangeIter(lo, hi)` -> iterator of keys in [lo, hi] INCLUSIVE, ascending; VERSION-
    STAMPED (structural OR value mutation mid-iteration throws). Bounds may be +-Infinity;
    NaN or lo > hi throws.
  - `size` / `capacity` / `alpha` getters; `clear()` -> this (empty, keep capacity);
    `forEach(fn)` visits (key, value, tree) ascending.
  - There is deliberately NO `split` / `merge` (the documented asymmetry vs Treap: no
    priority heap to merge by; an honest deterministic split/merge would be O(n) rebuilds).

- `MinMaxHeap` -- class. A DOUBLE-ENDED priority queue (DEPQ) in ONE array-embedded binary
  heap whose levels ALTERNATE min / max (Atkinson et al. 1986). The minimum is the root; the
  maximum is the larger of the root's up-to-two children. Two parallel typed-array columns
  (`_key` Float64, `_id` Uint32); the id is an OPAQUE Uint32 payload in [0, 2^32) (not unique,
  no reverse map). Keys are finite numbers (typeof-guarded before coercion; Symbol / BigInt /
  NaN / +-Infinity fail closed). Non-addressable: deliberately NO changeKey / remove.
  - `new MinMaxHeap(capacity)` -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^31-1]. Allocates the two typed
    arrays once. NO `kind` argument (a DEPQ serves both ends).
  - `push(id, key)` -> void. id integer in [0, 2^32); key finite. The key is checked FIRST,
    then the id, then a full heap; each throws `[lite-logn]` as a no-op (size unchanged).
  - `popMin()` -> id | undefined. Removes the minimum; undefined if empty (no throw).
  - `popMax()` -> id | undefined. Removes the maximum; undefined if empty (no throw).
  - `peekMin()` / `peekMax()` -> id | undefined. `peekMinKey()` / `peekMaxKey()` -> key |
    undefined. All O(1), read-only, undefined if empty (never throw).
  - `size` / `capacity` getters; `clear()`; `forEach(fn)` and `[Symbol.iterator]()` yield
    live ids in UNSPECIFIED (heap-array) order -- NOT sorted / pop order.
  - `MinMaxHeap.build(ids, keys, capacity)` -> MinMaxHeap. Floyd O(n) bulk build from parallel
    arrays (deepest-first, level-aware sift-down); fails closed on non-array-like / length
    mismatch, count > capacity, out-of-range id, or non-finite key.
- `SplayTree` -- class. A SELF-ADJUSTING BST ordered map (key -> value) via top-down splay;
  the LEAN member (no rank / select / split / merge).
  - `new SplayTree(capacity)` -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^31-1]. Allocates the four typed-
    array columns + the private free-list once; no seed argument (DETERMINISTIC, no RNG).
  - `get(key)` -> value | undefined. AMORTIZED O(log n). SPLAYS the touched key (or the last
    node on the search path) to the root and BUMPS the iteration version -- a read restructures.
  - `has(key)` -> boolean. AMORTIZED O(log n); SPLAYS + bumps version like get.
  - `set(key, value)` -> this. Insert, or update the value in place if key exists (splay the
    key up first). AMORTIZED O(log n). Fails closed on non-finite key/value or a full pool.
  - `delete(key)` -> boolean (idempotent). AMORTIZED O(log n): splay the target to the root,
    then JOIN its two subtrees (splay the max of the left subtree up, hang the right there).
  - `successor(key)` / `predecessor(key)` -> number | undefined. STRICT. AMORTIZED O(log n):
    each SPLAYS the closest node to `key` to the root and bumps the version.
  - `rangeIter(lo, hi)` -> IterableIterator<number>. Keys in [lo, hi] INCLUSIVE, ascending; a
    NON-splaying, VERSION-STAMPED in-order walk (leaves _root + _version byte-identical). Bounds
    may be +-Infinity; NaN or lo > hi throws; any mutation mid-iteration (INCLUDING a get/has,
    since reads splay) throws `[lite-logn]`.
  - `size` / `capacity` getters; `clear()` -> this; `forEach(fn)` and `[Symbol.iterator]()`
    are NON-splaying ascending-key walks (forEach passes (key, value, tree)).
- `BinomialHeap` -- class. The family's first MERGEABLE priority queue: a forest of binomial
  trees whose defining op is `meld` in O(log n). LEAN + NON-ADDRESSABLE (no decreaseKey /
  remove / rank / select); the id is an OPAQUE Uint32 payload in [0, 2^32).
  - `new BinomialHeap(capacity, kind = 'min')` -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^31-1]; kind
    'min' | 'max' frozen at construction. Owns its OWN arena (six columns + a private pool).
  - `BinomialHeap.arena(capacity, kind, count)` -> BinomialHeap[]. Builds `count` EMPTY heaps
    that SHARE one backing arena (pool + columns), so any two of them can meld. `capacity` is
    the arena-WIDE node budget. Fails closed on a bad capacity / kind / count (count integer >= 1).
  - `push(id, key)` -> void. O(1) AMORTIZED (O(log n) worst -- a binary carry). Fails closed:
    non-finite key (checked FIRST), out-of-range id, a full arena, or a consumed heap.
  - `popMin()` -> id | undefined. O(log n) worst; removes the extreme (min for a 'min' heap,
    max for a 'max' heap). undefined if empty (no throw). Consumed heap throws.
  - `peekMin()` -> id | undefined; `peekMinKey()` -> key | undefined. O(1) via the cached
    extreme root. undefined if empty. Consumed heap throws.
  - `meld(other)` -> this. O(log n): relink the two order-sorted root lists with a binary
    carry, folding every node of `other` into `this`. CONSUMES `other` (empty, size 0, DEAD --
    any later op on it throws). Fails closed: non-BinomialHeap arg, self-meld, cross-arena
    (column identity `this._key !== other._key`), kind mismatch, or a consumed operand.
  - `size` / `capacity` / `kind` getters; `clear()` -> this (frees only THIS heap's own nodes
    to the shared pool); `forEach(fn)` and `[Symbol.iterator]()` yield live ids in UNSPECIFIED
    (forest) order -- NOT sorted / pop order. Consumed heap throws on clear / forEach / iterate.
- `PairingHeap` -- class. The mergeable-heap arc's ADDRESSABLE priority queue: a single multi-way
  heap-ordered tree with an O(1) push/meld and an amortized-O(log n) cut-and-link decreaseKey /
  remove by id. LOUD CONTRACT: ids are UNIQUE ARENA-WIDE (integers in [0, capacity)); the reverse
  map is shared across every heap in the arena, and a per-slot owner tag makes decreaseKey/remove
  on a sibling heap's id an O(1) throw (fail closed) -- unlike BinomialHeap's opaque, non-unique,
  non-addressable ids.
  - `new PairingHeap(capacity, kind = 'min')` -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^31-1] (also the
    arena-wide id domain); kind 'min' | 'max' frozen at construction. Owns its OWN arena.
  - `PairingHeap.arena(capacity, kind, count)` -> PairingHeap[]. Builds `count` EMPTY heaps that
    SHARE one backing arena (pool + columns + arena-wide reverse map), so any two of them meld in
    O(1). `capacity` is the arena-WIDE node budget + id domain. Fails closed on a bad capacity /
    kind / count (count integer >= 1).
  - `push(id, key)` -> void. O(1) (a single root-link). Fails closed: non-finite key (checked
    FIRST), out-of-range id, an id live ANYWHERE in the arena (arena-wide uniqueness), a full
    arena, or a consumed heap.
  - `popMin()` -> id | undefined. AMORTIZED O(log n) (unlink root + TWO-PASS combine the child
    list, 0 B/op). undefined if empty (no throw). Consumed heap throws.
  - `peekMin()` -> id | undefined; `peekMinKey()` -> key | undefined. O(1) via the cached root.
    undefined if empty. Consumed heap throws.
  - `decreaseKey(id, newKey)` -> void. AMORTIZED O(log n): cut the subtree, link it at the root.
    Moves TOWARD the heap's extreme (decrease for 'min', increase for 'max'); a move away fails
    closed. Fails closed: non-finite key (FIRST), out-of-range / non-member id, a sibling-owned id
    (O(1) owner guard), or a consumed heap.
  - `remove(id)` -> boolean. AMORTIZED O(log n): cut + two-pass-combine children + link at root.
    true if present, false if absent. Fails closed: out-of-range id, a sibling-owned id, or a
    consumed heap.
  - `has(id)` -> boolean; `keyOf(id)` -> key | undefined. O(1) over the arena-wide reverse map
    (false / undefined for a sibling-owned or absent id). Out-of-range id / consumed heap throw.
  - `meld(other)` -> this. O(1): a single root-link + a union alias (INDEPENDENT of |other|,
    BETTER than BinomialHeap's O(log n) meld). CONSUMES `other` (empty, size 0, DEAD -- any later
    op on it throws); a melded-in id stays reprioritizable via `this`. Fails closed: non-PairingHeap
    arg, self-meld, cross-arena (column identity `this._key !== other._key`), kind mismatch, or a
    consumed operand.
  - `size` / `capacity` / `kind` getters; `clear()` -> this (frees only THIS heap's own nodes to
    the shared pool); `forEach(fn)` and `[Symbol.iterator]()` yield live ids in UNSPECIFIED
    (forest) order -- NOT sorted / pop order. Consumed heap throws on clear / forEach / iterate.
- `FibonacciHeap` -- class. The mergeable-heap arc's FINALE: the textbook-optimal ADDRESSABLE
  mergeable priority queue -- O(1)-amortized push/meld/decreaseKey (cascading cuts + a per-node mark
  bit), O(log n)-amortized popMin/remove (degree consolidation). Same ADDRESSABLE, arena-wide-unique
  id contract as PairingHeap. HONESTY: textbook-optimal asymptotics, but OFTEN slower wall-clock than
  Pairing/Binary here; shipped for completeness + teaching.
  - `new FibonacciHeap(capacity, kind = 'min')` -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^31-1] (also the
    arena-wide id domain); kind 'min' | 'max' frozen at construction. Owns its OWN arena.
  - `FibonacciHeap.arena(capacity, kind, count)` -> FibonacciHeap[]. Builds `count` EMPTY heaps that
    SHARE one backing arena (pool + columns + arena-wide reverse map + degree-bucket scratch), so any
    two of them meld in O(1). Fails closed on a bad capacity / kind / count (count integer >= 1).
  - `push(id, key)` -> void. O(1) AMORTIZED (a singleton splice into the root list). Fails closed:
    non-finite key (checked FIRST), out-of-range id, an id live ANYWHERE in the arena, a full arena,
    or a consumed heap.
  - `popMin()` -> id | undefined. AMORTIZED O(log n) (splice the min root's children into the root
    list, then CONSOLIDATE by degree, 0 B/op). undefined if empty (no throw). Consumed heap throws.
  - `peekMin()` -> id | undefined; `peekMinKey()` -> key | undefined. O(1) via the cached extreme.
    undefined if empty. Consumed heap throws.
  - `decreaseKey(id, newKey)` -> void. AMORTIZED O(1): lower the key; if heap order breaks, cut the
    subtree to the root and CASCADE up (marked ancestors cut too). Moves TOWARD the heap's extreme; a
    move away fails closed. Fails closed: non-finite key (FIRST), out-of-range / non-member id, a
    sibling-owned id (O(1) owner guard), or a consumed heap.
  - `remove(id)` -> boolean. AMORTIZED O(log n): cut + cascade + splice-children consolidation. true
    if present, false if absent. Fails closed: out-of-range id, a sibling-owned id, or a consumed heap.
  - `has(id)` -> boolean; `keyOf(id)` -> key | undefined. O(1) over the arena-wide reverse map.
    Out-of-range id / consumed heap throw.
  - `meld(other)` -> this. O(1): concatenate the two circular root lists + a union alias (INDEPENDENT
    of |other|, no per-node retag) + a cached-extreme update. CONSUMES `other` (empty, size 0, DEAD).
    Fails closed: non-FibonacciHeap arg, self-meld, cross-arena, kind mismatch, or a consumed operand.
  - `size` / `capacity` / `kind` getters; `clear()` -> this (frees only THIS heap's own nodes to the
    shared pool); `forEach(fn)` and `[Symbol.iterator]()` yield live ids in UNSPECIFIED (forest)
    order -- NOT sorted / pop order. Consumed heap throws on clear / forEach / iterate.
- `Fenwick2D` -- class. A 2D Fenwick tree (2D Binary Indexed Tree): BOTH point-update AND
  2D-prefix / rectangle-sum in O(log^2 n) over a single flat `Float64Array((rows+1)*(cols+1))` via
  the NESTED lowest-set-bit walk (`i & -i` on both dims). Public coords 0-based in
  [0, rows) x [0, cols); internally 1-based (row 0 / col 0 the unused identity sentinels). Values
  are finite numbers (negatives allowed); NaN / +-Infinity / non-number fail closed. SUM-ONLY and
  index-addressed (no 2D min / max / gcd, no changeKey / rank / select).
  - `new Fenwick2D(rows, cols)` -- rows, cols integers >= 1, frozen at ctor. Allocates one
    `Float64Array((rows+1)*(cols+1))`, zero-initialized. Throws when (rows+1)*(cols+1) exceeds
    `F2D_MAX_CELLS` (2^31-1), guarded by a float multiply (never `| 0`).
  - `rows` / `cols` getters. O(1).
  - `update(r, c, delta)` -> this. Add delta at 0-based (r, c) (climb both dims by `i & -i`); delta
    must be a finite number (typeof-guarded first); out-of-range coord throws.
  - `prefix(r, c)` -> number. Sum of the rectangle [0..r] x [0..c] INCLUSIVE. `prefix(-1, .)` and
    `prefix(., -1)` are 0 (the empty-prefix base case); valid domain [-1, rows) x [-1, cols).
  - `rectSum(r1, c1, r2, c2)` -> number. Sum of [r1..r2] x [c1..c2] INCLUSIVE on all four edges,
    via 2D inclusion-exclusion; throws on out-of-range or r1 > r2 / c1 > c2.
  - `at(r, c)` -> number. The single cell = the 1x1 rectangle sum.
  - `set(r, c, value)` -> this. Set cell (r, c) to value (absolute), via update(r, c, value -
    at(r, c)); value must be finite.
  - `clear()` -> this (zero-fill, keep dims); `forEach(fn)` visits (value, r, c, fenwick2d) in
    row-major ascending order (r outer, c inner).
  - `Fenwick2D.build(matrix)` -> Fenwick2D. O(rows*cols) LINEAR bulk build from a 2D array-like in
    TWO SEPARATE passes (cols within each row, then rows -- fusing them double-counts); fails closed
    on a non-2D-array-like, ragged rows, or any non-finite entry.
- `SegmentTree2D` -- class. A 2D segment tree (a segment tree OF segment trees): BOTH point-update
  AND a general rectangle FOLD (min / max / sum / gcd) in O(log^2 n) over a single flat
  `Float64Array(4 * rows * cols)` -- the exact rectangle MIN / MAX / GCD Fenwick2D cannot do. The
  fold is chosen ONCE at ctor. Public coords 0-based in [0, rows) x [0, cols). Values are finite
  numbers (NaN / +-Infinity / non-number fail closed typeof-first; the gcd kind also rejects
  negatives / non-integers). Correct ONLY for commutative + associative folds (order-agnostic 2n
  layout). SPACE co-headline: 4*rows*cols cells (~4x a 2D BIT).
  - `new SegmentTree2D(rows, cols, kind)` -- rows, cols integers >= 1, kind 'min'|'max'|'sum'|'gcd',
    frozen at ctor. Allocates one `Float64Array(4*rows*cols)` (filled with the fold identity for
    min/max). Throws when 4*rows*cols exceeds `S2D_MAX_CELLS` (2^31-1), guarded by a float multiply
    (never `| 0`, which would fail OPEN).
  - `rows` / `cols` / `kind` getters. O(1).
  - `query(r1, c1, r2, c2)` -> number. The fold over [r1..r2] x [c1..c2] INCLUSIVE on all four
    edges; throws on out-of-range or r1 > r2 / c1 > c2.
  - `update(r, c, value)` -> this. Set cell (r, c) to value (absolute), fixing every affected fold
    (inner col-tree then outer row-tree); value must be finite (nonnegative integer for gcd);
    out-of-range coord throws.
  - `at(r, c)` -> number. The single cell (the stored leaf value). O(1).
  - `clear()` -> this (reset to identity, keep dims/kind); `forEach(fn)` visits (value, r, c, tree)
    in row-major ascending order (r outer, c inner).
  - `SegmentTree2D.build(matrix, kind)` -> SegmentTree2D. O(rows*cols) two-phase bottom-up build
    from a 2D array-like (fold each row's col-tree, then fold the row-tree position-wise -- NOT
    rows*cols updates); fails closed on a non-2D-array-like, ragged rows, or any non-finite (or
    out-of-domain gcd) entry.

Member exports (one tree-shakeable class each) are appended here as each member
ships.

## Design bounds

- Zero runtime deps; node:test only; ASCII-only source.
- Single PascalCase main file LogN.js; sideEffects: false; tree-shakeable named
  exports, no barrel.
- Fixed, preallocated capacity (node / element count, not bytes). Fail closed on
  every unverified state; `null` is not zero.
- typeof-guard FIRST, before any coercion, at the door of every mutating op.
- Zero allocation on every steady-state hot path (0 B/op), proven by
  `node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs`.

## Cross-package boundaries

- @zakkster/lite-o1 -- the O(1) sibling and intended pair. Any BOUNDED-INTEGER
  priority queue is O(1) and belongs there (Dial's bucket queue); lite-logn's
  heap is the GENERAL comparator PQ at O(log n).
- @zakkster/lite-filter -- owns approximate / probabilistic membership;
  lite-logn owns exact ordered structures. No overlap.
